text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in the TP+PP job on 8xA100-int8 overnight. Latency p50 up ~18% and allreduce stalls spiking.

ajay: :eyes: which job/config? any flamegraphs?

maria: nightly-inference/tp-pipeline/int8-run. Attached profiler from perf-bot shows a big chunk in `allreduce_wait` during decode.

ken: can you paste the pprof snippet? rough numbers are enough.

maria: sure:
```
allreduce_wait_ms: 11.9
compute_ms: 7.2
kv_cache_lookup_ms: 3.4
batch_dispatch_ms: 2.1
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.61
```

lisa: kv hit rate 0.61 is low for the workload — are we seeing stale prefix caching because TP sharding changed seq assignments?

maria: maybe. We rolled kernel-selection changes yesterday that prefer fused-int8-gemm on attention blocks (new heuristic). Could be interacting with TP tensor slices.

ajay: that fused-int8 path was supposed to reduce compute, not increase allreduce waits. Hypothesis: int8 scaling on shard boundaries produces larger activation variance -> longer KV sizes (padding) -> bigger messages for allreduce and less overlap.

ken: also check whether continuous batching heuristics extended max_seq on some requests. If batcher groups a short+long and we don't trim padding per tensor-slice, message size blows up.

maria: repro plan: run small local reproduce with `./scripts/run_tp_profile.sh --model opt-6.7b --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 8 --quant int8 --trace` and compare with `--quant fp8` and `--kernel=legacy-gemm`

lisa: also dump the KV shapes per-rank, e.g., in runtime add logging: `kv_cache.shape()` per layer per decode step. put into /tmp/prof-<run>.json

perf-bot: nightly-inference/tp-pipeline/int8-run failed perf-threshold check. Artifacts: https://internal/prof/1968000123/ (pprof + timeline) :warning:

ajay: I looked at the timeline — there's a tight window where compute finishes early but ranks are stalled waiting for allreduce. Overlap seems poor: network pendings not kicked off until later on some ranks. Looks like kernel change moved CUDA streams ordering.

ken: yep — fused kernel created a synchronous copy on rank boundary (we missed an async path). If kernel uses default stream instead of per-stream comms, NCCL kicks in later -> loss of overlap.

maria: that explains the allreduce_wait bump. Why kv hit rate drops though?

lisa: sequence: larger effective sequence (padding) -> more KV mem read, but if shards reorder requests for batching, some ranks see cache misses because offsets don't align. TP tensor slicing + int8 fused path might change the order of requests entering the KV cache loop.

ajay: quick mitigation: force `kernel_selection: allow_async_comm=false` -> roll back to earlier behavior; patch batching to `max_padding_tokens=64` to avoid huge messages. Try falling back to `fp8` for attention layers > 32K weights.

maria: i'll queue a canary with those two changes on dedicated 2-node cluster.

ken: we should also add a guard in kernel selector: when TP>1 and quant=int8, prefer kernel variant that exposes separate comm stream (tag: `comm_safe`) until we audit async-calls.

lisa: regarding numeric drift, we've seen int8 scaling mismatch at shard boundaries before. Add a quick eval with `eval-set/kv-regress` to detect generation drift if we switch kernels.

maria: logs from canary run (early):
```
[rank0] kernel=ip-int8-fused comm_stream=default
[rank1] kernel=ip-int8-fused comm_stream=default
allreduce_wait_ms: 13.7
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.59
```

maria: after forcing comm-safe kernel:
```
[rank0] kernel=ip-int8-commsafe comm_stream=async0
[rank1] kernel=ip-int8-commsafe comm_stream=async1
allreduce_wait_ms: 4.8
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.63
```

ajay: nice delta. But need to ensure commsafe variant doesn't regress quality. Run int8 vs fp8 short evals and also run throughput test.

ken: assign action items:
- maria: run 3 canary runs (int8+commsafe, int8+legacy, fp8) and upload pprof + KV shapes (due EOD).
- ajay: add kernel_selector rule to prefer `comm_safe` on TP>1 & quant=int8; add unit test for stream ordering.
- lisa: create kv-shape quickcheck and add to nightly smoke (fail if hit_rate < 0.7).

maria: added labels in CI: `ci-agent:trigger:tp-int8-smoke` -> starting first run now :rocket:

ci-agent: queued job `tp-int8-smoke-1968000123-1` on node set `dedicated-2x-a100`, ETA ~12m

ajay: follow-up — let's also add a microbenchmark that simulates TP-sharded allreduce sizes so we can tune batching heuristics without whole-model runs.

lisa: agreed. I'll sketch the microbench today and ping for review.

ken: one more note — if we fallback to commsafe kernels long-term, we should document cost tradeoffs. commsafe might slightly increase compute due to extra kernel paths but saves on stall latency.

maria: ok, I'll post results and open a PR with the selector change if canary looks good. thanks team :thumbsup:

ajay: :partyparrot: great investigation, very actionable.
